Robert Bates, an Oklahoma reserve deputy charged with second-degree manslaughter in the death of Eric Harris, has released training documents to verify his qualifications. His lawyer, Scott Wood, argues Bates met all required training standards, including one Taser class and multiple firearms qualifications, though the Tulsa County Sheriff's Office has disputed the records' authenticity. The documents are central to the case, as the victim's family claims Bates received preferential treatment despite inadequate training.

A naturalized U.S. citizen from Columbus was arraigned Friday on federal charges of providing material support to terrorists and lying to the FBI. Abdirahman Sheik Mohamud, 23, allegedly traveled to Syria in 2014 for training and plotted to return home and kill Americans, particularly U.S. soldiers. Mohamud was remanded into custody and his lawyer says he will get a vigorous defense.

However, depression can sometimes manifest during a career, though it is treatable and no longer debilitating to a pilot's livelihood under new FAA regulations. This week's pop culture highlights include the release of a new "Star Wars" trailer featuring Harrison Ford and Chewbacca, a viral logic puzzle about Cheryl's birthday, and ESPN reporter Britt McHenry's awkward on-air mistake. Additionally, "Late Late Show" host Jon Cryer recreated a classic dance routine, while Gisele Bündchen retired from the runway and a new book explores the toxicity of online shaming.

Warner Bros. and director Michelle MacLaren have parted ways over "creative differences" just weeks before the start of production on the "Wonder Woman" film. The studio will now search for a new director to replace MacLaren, who was announced in November, as Gal Gadot's solo outing remains slated for a June 23, 2017 release.

Hernandez confessed to the crime in 2012, claiming he lured Patz into a basement, but his lawyer argues he is mentally incompetous and unable to discern if he actually committed the crime. A judge previously ruled Hernandez's confession admissible, yet the case remains fraught with questions about his mental state and the lack of physical evidence, as the Patz family seeks justice decades after their son's disappearance.

ABC is developing a revival of "The Muppets" at the upfront presentation. Bill Prady co-writes the pilot, with Bob Kushell attached as showrunner. The project moves forward only if Miss Piggy signs on, as her current relationship with Kermit is reportedly preventing the show from getting off the ground. If ordered to series, Prady would juggle the project with his duties on "The Big Bang Theory."

Decades later, she continues to hear similar stories of women and girls being harassed on public transport and in other public spaces, noting that 80% of women in Mumbai have been street harassed, primarily in crowded areas like trains and railway platforms. Many women limit their hours outside, select more conservative clothes, or opt for a longer but safer route home, and most people are silent when inappropriate sexual behavior occurs to women.

Canadian actor Jonathan Crombie, best known for playing Gilbert Blythe in the "Anne of Green Gables" TV movies, died at age 48 from brain hemorrhage complications. His role opposite Megan Follows became a cultural touchstone, spinning off into a beloved character for fans worldwide. The "Anne of Green Gables" alum passed away Wednesday, leaving behind a legacy of "boy-next-door" charm and "amazing chemistry" with his on-screen wife.

Al-Shabaab's latest attack on Garissa University College, which left 147 dead, represents the deadliest assault in Kenya within the past year and a half. The group, affiliated with al Qaeda, has steadily been losing ground in Somalia because of African Union forces and U drone strikes, yet they still target "soft targets" like universities and malls to protest the extra 3,500 Kenyan soldiers participating in the African Union peacekeeping mission in Somalia.

In addition to that ruling, Judge Ronald Coen also lowered Knight's bail to $10 million from $25 million, a figure that defense lawyers called excessive. The judge also dismissed one of the two counts of hit-and-run against Knight. National Park Week, running from April 18 to 26, offers free admission to the 128 U.S. national parks that typically charge fees, including Yellowstone and Yosemite. The initiative, hosted by the National Park Service and the National Park Foundation, features events like astronomy parties and Junior Ranger activities to encourage public exploration. The service encourages visitors to share their experiences using the hashtag #FindYourPark.

CNN reports on the affordable housing crisis in Silicon Valley, highlighting families like Nicole paying $1,000 monthly for a one-car garage, while nationally 7.7 million low-income households spend over half their income on rent, threatening economic stability and children's futures.

An American citizen was shot multiple times while driving in Karachi, Pakistan, on Thursday. Debra Lobo, a 55-year-old California native, was wounded in the cheek and arm but is expected to survive after being attacked by two assailants on a motorcycle. Police are investigating the incident, which is believed to be linked to anti-American sentiments, and the U.S. Consulate General is assisting Pakistani authorities.

A jury of Rolling Stone's media peers has determined that the magazine's discredited rape story amounted to journalistic malpractice, citing "startling lapses" in basic reporting standards. The report found that Sabrina Erdely never verified her key source's identity, refused to give the fraternity a fair chance to respond, and ignored red flags from Jackie, ultimately publishing a story that sparked nationwide debate but was und verable from the start.

Jon Cryer reprised his iconic record-store dance from "Pretty on the Outside" on "The Late Late Show," dancing alongside host James Corden. The recreation fulfilled Corden's childhood dream, as the duo performed the routine to Otis Redding's "Try a Little Tenderness" in front of a record store audience. Many original fans of the 1986 John Hughes film, now middle-aged, still celebrated the nostalgic moment.

As poll watchers, they knew most Americans oppose discriminatory laws, but politicians underestimated business backlash. Ines Dumig's photo series "Apart Together" documents Sahra, a Somali refugee navigating the asylum process in Germany. Dumig was drawn to Sahra's strength and her reflection on her past experiences, and the project serves as a broader story about displacement and identity. The work highlights the universal feelings of isolation and "otherness" that link people together, emphasizing that despite physical separation, shared human emotions connect us.

Jarret Stoll of the L.A. Kings was arrested Friday at a Las Vegas resort pool on a drug-possession charge. He was released on $5,000 bail, while the Kings have launched an internal investigation into the incident. The 32-year-old center, who has been with the team since 2008, was charged with possession of cocaine and ecstasy.

Police in Marana, Arizona, initially believed a shoplifting suspect's gun was locked and unable to fire, but 10 seconds after being informed otherwise, the suspect fired a shot into the air. A police officer then struck the suspect with his patrol car, ending a crime spree and leading to his arrest. The 36-year-old suspect is now facing 15 charges, including shoplifting a rifle, and is scheduled to appear in court on May 18.

Two Delaware boys are in a coma and their father is unable to move two weeks after they fell ill on a trip to the U.V.I., possibly from pesticide exposure. The family was airlifted to U.S. hospitals after staying at the Sirenusa resort in St. John; the boys, 16 and 14, are in critical condition, while the father is conscious but cannot move and the mother is in occupational therapy. The EPA found methyl bromide in the villa and is investigating if the family was made ill after a fumigation on March 18.

A suicide car bomb attack near the U.S. Consulate in Irbil, Iraq, was claimed by ISIS. At least four people were killed and 18 injured, though all U.S. personnel were reported safe. The blast, which occurred close to civilian and expat-favorite businesses, underscores the ongoing threat of terrorism in the region.

Over 300 suspects have been arrested in South Africa following deadly attacks on foreigners that killed at least five people and forced thousands to flee. The government condemned the violence, praising police for preventing further bloodshed, while expressing that the unrest does not represent the views of all citizens. Officials have implored residents to remember the nation's history of seeking refuge, as the charity assisting refugees warned the situation remained desperate.

Davion Navar Henry Only, who spent his entire childhood in foster care, was finally adopted in April after a viral video of his 2013 adoption plea caught the attention of a minister's family in Ohio. Despite an initial rejection due to a conflict with the family's son, social worker Connie Going ultimately agreed to adopt him, moving into her home along with her three children just days before his official adoption date in April 22.

Saudi Arabia has been bombing Yemen for three weeks to prevent Houthi rebels from seeding regional dominance, though the conflict has caused a humanitarian crisis with over 600 killed and 2,000 wounded, as civilians flee the violence.

Joy Womack, a former Bolshoi Ballet Academy student, has been dancing at the Kremlin Ballet Theatre since 2013. While she performs principal roles near the Russian president's office, she receives a monthly salary of approximately $240, translating to about $8 a day. Womack attributes this financial struggle to the weakening ruble, caused by low oil prices and international sanctions, forcing her to rely on a bank account of $185 and additional performances abroad to make ends meet.

Six Minnesota men, aged 19 to 21, were arrested for conspirating to join ISIS in Syria. The group plotted for ten months, recruiting each other in a peer-to-peer fashion. Four appeared in court Monday, with a judge ordering them held without bail as they attempt to leave the U.S. to fight for a terror group.

Dr. Sanjay Gupta explores the evolving landscape of medical marijuana in "Weed 3: The Marijuana Revolution," addressing its potential to treat conditions like epilepsy and multiple sclerosis while acknowledging the historical misinformation and brain development concerns that have long kept the subject taboo in the medical community. After extensive research, Gupta admits he changed his mind on the drug, highlighting its potential benefits for patients reliant on painkillers and those suffering from PTSD, while referencing legitimate long-term concerns regarding brain function.

While working with Nepalese refugees in India, she met a young girl searching for family, witnessing the aftermath of a decade-long civil war. Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a frozen pizza business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in their Wisconsin town. A complete camel skeleton was found under a cellar in Tulln, Austria. Archaeologists from the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna discovered it during a construction project from 2006 to 2007. At first, the remains were thought to be a large horse or cattle. However, the shape of the neck bones, jaw, and foot bones showed it was actually a camel.

Andrew Getty, the 47-year-old grandson of J. Paul Getty, died at his home in Los Angeles on Tuesday. His parents, Ann and Gordon Getty, asked the media and the public to respect their privacy during this difficult time.

We might never understand why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9525 into the French Alps on March 24, killing everyone on board. Lousanne, Switzerland (CNN) -- A series of talks ended Thursday in Lausanne. A group of world powers known as the P5+1 reached a framework agreement with Iran over the country's nuclear program. The success of the deal is uncertain. The parties have until the end of June to work out the details and put the plan in paper. But the talks this week were historic, particularly for the otherwise frozen U.S.-Iranian relationship. However, the negotiations were not glamorous. In fact, the talks provided a modern demonstration of diplomacy at its best, but also at its most hectic.

A bomb exploded near a United Nations vehicle in northeastern Somalia on Monday morning, killing six people. This included four aid workers from the UNICEF agency. Somalia's President called it an attack on the country's future. The attack happened about 8 a.m. in the administrative capital of the Puntland region. This follows a separate incident on Sunday where three African Union troops died in an ambush. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack.

CNN reports that Britain's Prince Harry arrived in Australia on Monday. He will spend four weeks with the country's military. Before starting his duty, the 30-year-old prince visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra. He paid respect to the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier. A crowd of onlookers gathered there. Some took photos, and a boy held a sign that read "Red Heads Rule!" The Australian Defence Forces say Prince Harry will work and live with colleagues in the Army in regiments in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth.

Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said the deal is an "informal arrangement" focused on tracking Australians traveling to Iraq to fight ISIS. One lawmaker called the move " dancing with the devil." Over the weekend, Bishop became the first Australian minister to visit Iran in 12 years, meeting President Rouhani. The intelligence-sharing deal was announced in an interview Bishop gave to Australian media while in Tehran.

A BEA statement from Friday says its teams have started to investigate the device's contents.

A 110-day chase that started near Antarctica and ended off the coast of west Africa had an unexpected conclusion when the crew of a suspected poaching ship were rescued by conservationists. The environmentalist group Sea Shepherd had been following the Thunder -- a ship Interpol says is wanted for suspected fraud and fisheries-related crimes -- since the Bob Barker encountered it in the Southern Ocean several months ago. The pursuit ended early Monday in the Gulf of Guinea, off the coast of west Africa, when the Bob Barker received a distress call from the Thunder.

More than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls disappeared from their boarding school in Chibok exactly one year ago. They are still missing. The world should feel that young girls can be kidnapped so easily by extremists, and that we have forgotten about this tragedy.

When more than 200 Nigerian girls were kidnapped from their school a year ago by Boko Haram militants, millions of people around the world joined a social media campaign to plead for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of those people -- from celebrities to world leaders -- voicing their anger via #BringBackOurGirls, one of the top Twitter hashtags of 2014, used in more than four million tweets. But as weeks turned into months, there was still no sign of the missing girls. The spotlight on the campaign faded.

CNN reports that Barney Frank, a retired congressman, recently spoke in Chicago. He entertained a sold-out crowd at the Center on Halsted by sharing stories from his 45-year career in public service. Frank made history as the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same-sex while in office. When asked about a California ballot proposal that would legalize killing gay people, he admitted he wasn't aware of the measure but advised the young man not to "worry yourself about the crazy people."

A brutal attack at Garissa University College in Kenya has left nearly 150 people dead, including students, and dozens more wounded. Gunmen attacked the campus early Thursday while morning prayers were happening, shooting randomly and taking hostages before being killed by security forces. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said that Al-Shabaab militants claimed responsibility. This harsh attack comes just months after Al-Shabaab militants murdered non-Muslim workers in a Kenyan quarry. The terrorist group has been behind numerous attacks in the region. It has also recruited some Americans, particularly from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

A South African university is taking down a statue of a British colonialist after weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town started a campaign on social media last month demanding the statue of Cecil Rhodes come down, saying his legacy is tainted with racism. Using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall, the students demanded the removal. Four weeks later, the hashtag is now #RhodesHas Fallen. The university said Wednesday the heritage authority granted it permission to remove the statue from the campus. "These steps are being taken to ensure the safety of the statue while matters concerning its future are resolved," the university said in a statement.

Syria is a very dangerous place. An opposition group says the number of people who have died there has doubled in one year. Since the civil war started, 310,000 people have been killed, according to a group that watches human rights. One year ago, the number was 162,402. The United Nations says the number was 70,000 two years ago.

The United Nations also says that violence has pushed more than half of all Syrians into poverty. They are so poor they need help to survive. This is happening because food rations have been cut because not enough people are donating food.

CNN reports that Ailina Tsarnaeva was not silent or shy when it came to threatening a woman. According to a criminal complaint, she called the woman and said, "Leave my man alone." She also threatened, "Stop looking for him. I know people that can put a bomb where you live." Prosecutors took these threats seriously and charged her with aggravated harassment, a charge she denies. She is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

CNN reports that a door with a drawing by the artist Banksy was taken by police in Gaza on Thursday. The door's owner, Rabea Darduna, said he sold it for only $175 because he did not know it was valuable. His home was destroyed last summer, and leaving him with only the door. The door is now held by the Khan Younis police in southern Gaza until a court hearing.

A Saudi-led coalition is attacking Houthi rebels in Yemen. Five days into the attacks, the coalition has destroyed most of the rebels' air defense systems and air bases. Saudi Arabia's navy is blocking Yemeni ports, only allowing closely watched non-military medical supplies to enter. Locals are fleeing the fighting, and the death toll is rising, including many civilians.

Holland manager Guus Hiddink was very angry after his own fans booed Spanish player Andres Iniesta. He called the fans a "disgrace." Spain coach Vicente del Bosque made some changes to the team. Iniesta came into the game in the 76th minute, but the home fans jeered and booed him. Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen scored first-half goals for Holland. Spain lost the game 2-0.

Scotland will find out on May 21 if their Euro 2016 qualifier with Georgia will be played with no fans in the stands. UEFA, European football's governing body, has started disciplinary proceedings against the Georgian Football Federation. This happened after fans twice invaded the pitch during Sunday's 2-0 defeat by Germany in Tbilisi. UEFA is also set to look at charges that allege home fans were guilty of setting off fireworks. They are also looking at safety breaches. These include blocked stairs, locked gates, and a lack of body searches by staff at the Boris Paichadze Stadium. A fan invodes the pitch during Georgia's 2-0 defeat by Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi.

Football agents were left waiting on Wednesday after new rules were announced. Starting April 1, anyone can become an agent by paying a £500 fee for a one-year registration. The FA will then charge £250 every year to renew the license. Agents who already had a license were exempt from these new rules. The FA was supposed to put a link on their website for agents to register, but as of 1pm it was still not there. Mel Stein thinks the new rules will cause chaos. These new guidelines came in after FIFA decided to stop governing agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, has not been paid for three months. He had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent.

Despite this financial issue, Uvarenko, who joined the club on an 18-month contract in January, is impressed by the fans and their support.

He told local media that the lack of money is the biggest problem he has faced at CSKA. He has not received his salary since joining the club in January.

David Moore, 25, got angry on the road after leaving his home and immediately got stuck in heavy traffic with Rafal Cegielka, 45, who was picking up his child from St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire. Moore then punched Cegielka and smashed up his car with a hockey stick in front of the children because he was having a "bad day" and saw red.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This game brought back bad memories of Spain's poor performance in the 2014 World Cup. However, coach Vicente del Bosque is not worried about a third straight friendly defeat, says Gerard Pique. Holland, known for its 5-1 victory over Spain in last year's group stage in Brazil, scored two early goals and held on against some determined Spain pressure in the second half for a 2-0 success.

A New York City mother and named Ulrike Berger has fled to Germany with her daughter during a custody battle, police claim. Ulrike Berger, 44, is not allowed by a court order from leaving the country with her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia. But on March 22, a day after the little girl was dropped off for a weekend visit, they are believed to have boarded a plane to Europe. Police are searching for Ulrike Berger, 44, and her seven-year-old daughter Kaia. It is believed the pair boarded a plane from New York to Germany on March 22, breaking a custody court order. Strong winds and dry weather caused a massive wildfire near the south coast. The fire burned through about 70 hectares of heathland—roughly the size of 100 football pitches. The fire started deliberately, and firefighters put out three separate areas, some as small as half a hectare. The damage came after several days of storms had felled trees and shut roads in Britain.

Last night, emergency services were overwhelmed with 600 calls every hour as people celebrated the New Year. Ambulances were stretched to their limit, and in Cambridge, a military field hospital was set up to treat drunk partys. At the peak, London's ambulance service was handling over 600 calls per hour—more than three times the normal amount. In Manchester, a man collapsed on the pavement next to an ambulance while revellers walked by eating takeaways, and another man was slumped over in a doorway as people celebrated.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet says his mental strength helped him recover after he was dropped in December. Mignolet was dropped indefinitely by manager Brendan Rodgers because his form was poor. He quickly returned when Brad Jones got a thigh injury. The 27-year-old Belgian said he tried to stay upbeat despite the disappointment.

Giant hailstones the size of plums crashed down over the South on Tuesday with residents rushing out to capture the freak weather. Twitter user Arke USA from Bryant, Arkansas, filmed the ice balls peppering his backyard and noisily plopping into the swimming pool. Footage shows the hailstones coming down at speed, with many cracking as they hit the ground. Despite it being around 80-degrees, the compacted lumps prove resilient to the heat taking a good while to melt. In a matter of seconds the patio is completely covered in snow-white pellets.

A replica pirate ship ran into trouble about 30 miles off the coast of Maine. The ship, called the Liana's Ransom, lost power in rough seas on Monday. The crew tried to fix the engine, but the sails got wrapped around the mast.

By Tuesday, the Coast Guard rescued nine people from the ship using small life boats. The ship was left adadrift at sea.

Amazing pictures have emerged of blue fluorescent algae lighting up Australia's east coast. The images were taken in Jervis Bay, the south coast of NSW, as the neon glow illuminated one of Australia's popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson described the sight as a 'beeful supernatural scene' caused by millions of plankton omitting light. A similar display was shown in Sydney's Manly Beach back in August 2014 where an oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia there was no need to be concerned about the algae.

A teenage boy named Rahul Kumar, 17, climbed into the lions' enclosure at a zoo in Ahmedabad, India. He was drunk and began running towards the animals, shouting that he would kill them. Zoo security had to rescue him.

A 12-year-old boy fell out of a five-story window and survived by landing on a car parked below. His father said the boy most likely fell while sleepwalking. The incident happened last Saturday in Nanchang, China. A hotel worker across the road heard a loud bang around midnight and thought it was a car accident.

Red Wings player Drew Miller is happy to be back on the ice just one day after getting a deep cut to his face. He feels very lucky the skate didn't hit his eye. Miller had a bad-looking gashhed wound that needed 50 to 60 stitches to close. He has a scar across his eye, but doctors say he didn't lose any eyesight.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid wants to sign him back in the summer. He signed a three-year deal last July but has struggled to keep his place at left-back. Atletico hope this might give them an advantage, but Luis said: 'I'm happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until the end of my contract.'

A Reading fan named Charlie Sumner got a three-year ban from football. He ran onto the pitch topless and did flips during his first game at Madejski Stadium last month. Sumner, who was 3-0 up with his team, did four front flips before stewards stopped him. He said going to the game was a 'brilliant experience'.

A video shows a group of men riding on top of a van as it swerved around a corner. About half a dozen people were sitting on the roof of the vehicle on a road near the coastal city of Salé, Morocco when it toppled on to one side at high speed. Terrifying footage of the incident was taken from a car following the van, which is understood to have been transporting football fans. The video shows the moment the packed vehicle starts to swerve from side-to-side on what appears to be a dual carriageway.

England have been drawn in Group D with the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy at the UEFA Under 17 European Championships in Bulgaria this May.

The team, managed by John Peacock, are the defending champions. They won last year's final in Malta against Holland on penalties. To defend their title, they must overcome the Dutch again to succeed to the quarter-finals.

This tournament has been expanded from eight to sixteen nations for the first time.

An annoyed elephant tried to spray a bull with water because the animal got too close. The elephant was relaxing in South Africa's Kruger National Park with its family by a small pool when the bull approached. In a photo, the elephant squits water from its trunk to make the bull leave, but missed. A frustrated elephant tries to spray the bull, which wandered too close. Its young calf cuddles up to its parent for protection while the bull drinks from the pool.

Michael Thorpe was convicted in 2006 for showing a Premier League game at his pub in Devon. He spent eight years fighting to clear his name. Yesterday, his conviction was overturned, but he has lost his pub in the process.

The Irish Football Association is worried that damage at their home in Belfast might stop the June game against Romania. Cracks were found in the West Stand on Tuesday morning. The area was closed off while engineers checked the damage. The Irish FA found out on Tuesday morning that overnight damage happened to the West Stand at Windsor Park.

A 20-year-old football fan ran onto the pitch at Reading's Madejski Stadium during a game last month. He did four front flips while the team was winning 3-0. He was then caught by security guards and banned for three years.

A BMW driver with five children was arrested after a student was killed while walking to the library. Hina Shamim, 21, died near Kingston University in London. She was just weeks away from her 22nd birthday. Friends left flowers at the scene. They said she was "much-loved and the most charming lovely girl in the world." Hina Shamim was killed after she was knocked down while walking home to the library.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video of them fighting with a student at a high school was posted online. The pair were at Langham Creek High School in Houston on Tuesday. The mother was angry with the student because she had allegedly been bullying her daughter. In the video, the mother is seen wearing a black top on the right side, and the student is in the center wearing white.

The chief executive of Stoke, Tony Scholes, is hopeful they can keep their goalkeeper, Asmir Begovic, even though his contract is about to end. Begovic has often been linked with other clubs. Although he has just over 12 months left on his deal, Scholes believes they can match the 27-year-old's ambitions. 'Clearly Asmir is a terrific goalkeeper and we are very keen to keep him at the club,' he said. 'I think when you've got extremely good players it is only natural that there will be speculation about their future.'

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand was filmed reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger sent the video to the bus company Ritchies Coachlines to complain. In the video, the driver can be seen turning pages of the newspaper while the bus is moving. When the bus slows down for a red light, he moves his head to get a better look at the paper. The boss at Ritchies Coachlines, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver's actions and called him a "complete idiot."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says Winston Reid will play against Leicester City on Saturday. Reid hurt his hamstring in a game against Chelsea on March 4, but he is now fully fit after returning to training during the international break.

Enner Valencia will not play. He missed the last two games after a toe injury at home in mid-Mrch, but Allardyce says he is still not match fit.

Five days before their wedding last May, Brittany Huber and John Redman were in a terrible car crash on a Georgia highway. Brittany died at the scene, and John was critically injured. Doctors told the 25-year-old assistant basketball coach that he would likely spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, confined to a wheelchair.

Again doctors said Redman would never recover, but against all odds, he got better. On March 24, he helped lead his team to a championship title.

Lucas (left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard during Sunday's All-Star charity game at Anfield. Liverpool midfielder Lucas Leiva is looking to recapture what he considers his best form in two years after recovering from injury. The Brazil international enjoyed a run of 16 starts in 19 matches from late November - which coincided with a marked improvement in the team's results - until a groin problem in February's Merseyside derby saw him miss 10 games. He was an unused substitute in the defeat by Manchester United immediately before the international break, their first in the league since mid-December, but played 90 minutes in Sunday's All-Star Charity game at Anfield.

Sick of awkward father-daughter photos? A Japanese photographer named Yûki Aoyama has found a funny way to make them better. In the photos, fathers are jumping into the air while their daughters stay on the ground with a smile. The daughter looks at the camera and smiles, while the father strikes a dramatic pose. These photos are from the photographer's new book, which roughly translates to "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old who robbed a bank in broad daylight and ran off with £3,000 in cash. The robbery happened at 12:30pm at a Lloyds Bank branch in Fairwater, Cardiff. Detectives have released CCTV images of the suspect. He is between 5ft 9in and 6ft tall, was wearing black clothing, and has greying black hair and wore glasses. The white male suspect was captured on camera inside the bank. Detectives said no one was injured during the robbery and they were 'confident' the public would be able to identify the suspect.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has lifted Morocco's ban from the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. The Confederation of African Football had originally banned Morocco from the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and fined the country $1 million. The CAF had also demanded an additional $9 million in compensation because Morocco pulled out due to fears related to the Ebola epidemic. Morocco can now compete in the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments.

Tom Boyd says Jason Denayer’s successful loan at Celtic means he is ready to play for Manchester City next season. This would make Ronny Deila want to keep Denayer for another year, but Boyd thinks it is still a good thing. Boyd believes Denayer’s success will encourage other young players to join Celtic. Jason Denayer, 19, has played well on loan at Celtic. He recently got his first cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England, silencing people who doubted him. This great season has been up and down for the 23-year-old, who has not played as well as he did when he first started on the international scene. England manager Roy Hodgson believed in Townsend, and Townsend re repaid that belief with an excellent goal at the Juventus Stadium. On Tuesday night, Townsend scored England's equal goal in their 1-1 friendly draw with Italy in Turin. Townsend celebrated his strike with Tottenham Hotspur team-mates Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. The purchase was finalized at a special meeting on Tuesday, where the legal team representing Wanda Madrid Investment approved buying 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8m). The deal was first announced in January, but two meetings were needed to finalize it. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin hopes to grow Atletico's brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone speaks to the media.

Antonio Conte returned to Turin for Italy's 1-1 draw against England. He said the trip brought "very fond memories," despite reports he received death threats before the friendly.

Conte took the Italy job in August after the team's poor World Cup performance. His first seven months in charge have been difficult. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to rescue a 2-2 draw against Bulgaria last Saturday. Reports also say Conte received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio suffered a knee injury before the Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that Hibs can catch Rangers for second place. His team, Dumbarton, have played both Rangers and Hibs already this season. Murray believes Rangers will find it hard to keep their winning form, and that Hibs might overt them before the season ends.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet returned to England after playing for Belgium in World Cup qualifying games. Even though he was on the team list for both games, he did not get to play. Chelsea's Thibaut Courtois was chosen instead. Mignolet shared photos of him sitting in a pilot's cockpit on Facebook.

A large rural estate is for sale for £6 million. The property, called Chyknell Hall Estate, is near Bridgnorth in Shropshire. It sits on 200 acres of land and includes a Grade II-listed manor house and five cottages.

The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms. It was built in 1814 and has only been sold twice before. The estate also has a swimming pool, a tennis court, stables, and its own cricket green. Exper think the secluded home could attract A-list buyers because the grounds offer complete privacy.

Two college campus police officers in Dallas have been placed on leave after video showed them harassing a group of students and hitting one man. The incident happened at El Centro College last Wednesday. A student named Charles Adams recorded the video while waiting for a bus outside the downtown campus.

Kilmarnock has made Gary Locke their permanent manager. The 39-year-old, who has only lost once in his last seven games, signed a three-year contract. He took the job temporarily in February when Allan Johnston quit, and has now been given the role full-time after a successful spell in charge.

This weekend, one of the biggest games on the German football calendar takes place. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five league titles between them, and Bayern are expected to continue their dominance this season.

Usually called "Der Klassiker," this match usually sees the two giants level at the top of the table. However, this time they are separated by nine points and 31 points in the standings. Even though the gap is big, the stakes are still as high as they always are when these two clubs meet.

Jurgen Klopp ( centre) celebrated with his Borussia Dortmund players after their victory against Hannover .

A 14-year-old girl was left stuck at London Stansted airport after easyJet refused to let her on her plane. She only had two pieces of hand luggage, which the airline would not allow. She offered to pay to store the second bag, but was told only credit cards could be used. She does not have a credit card.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed John Potts, 45, with one punch to the back of the head outside a sports bar. Robson had been drinking heavily after his grandfather's funeral. The punch was so hard it made an audible crack, and Mr. Potts fell down and died. Robson, who has a history of violent offenses, was sentenced to three and a and a half years in jail.

Ellen White scored a free kick against her old team, Arsenal. She hit the ball into the corner while her teammates Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood accidentally ran into each other, causing confusion at the free kick.

These are the amazing scenes as high school girls in China are put through their paces with military-style dagger drills. Each of the girls shout the words 'kill, stab, slash and jab' as they perform each of the eight set movements involved in the high-intensity knife-fighting session. According to the People's Daily Online, the girls of the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School are being trained by former special forces soldier Inspector Tan. The 68 girls involved in the training are all aged between 16 and 18, however in a concession to safety, the knives are not real. School official Huang Anruo said: 'The daggers are fake.'

We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping. However, many people do not realize how much sleep their mind and body need to feel refreshed every day. According to the Sleep Health Foundation, 30 percent of Australians complain about not getting enough sleep daily. Professor David Hillman says that these "lost" hours of sleep must be "paid back" to function properly throughout the week. A study shows that the average adult needs about eight hours of sleep per night, with a recommended range of seven to nine hours.

A video posted on Facebook shows a heated argument between neighbours in a Perth suburb. The argument escalated when a woman went into her neighbour's yard and brandished a metal crowbar, shouting racist slurs and swinging the weapon at a group of men. The men then picked up their own weapons and a scfuble broke out.

Everyone is watching 19-year-old Valencia left back Jose Luis Gaya. Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea want to sign him this summer. Sportsmail writer Pete Jensen looks at the Spain Under 21 defender. Why want English clubs so keen? His buy-out clause is currently set at £13.5m. When you consider that Luke Shaw – of a similar age and potential – cost £27m it would be silly not to be interested; although there would be also be reservations about his suitability to the Premier League. Jose Luis Gaya (right) in action for Valencia during a La Liga match with Sevilla earlier this season.
Police in Oregon are asking the public for help finding a man on a green motorcycle. He saved two teens after a 59-year-old man allegedly threatened them with a gun in Salem.

Tim Sherwood wants Ron Vlaar to play well so Aston Villa can avoid being relegated. Sherwood wants to see the fit defender help the team finish strongly. Vlaar played well for Holland in the World Cup in Brazil last year, even though he missed a penalty in a shoot-out against Argentina. This move could lead to links with Manchester United. Aston Villa will welcome back their club captain Ron Vlaar as they head to Old Trafford on Saturday. The commanding Dutch centre-back returns from injury to help Villa in their battle against relegation.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about a possible takeover of Aston Villa. He plans to build his own team next season if the team stays up in the league. Randy Lerner is in talks to sell the club. If a new owner takes over, questions about Sherwood's job will come up. But Sherwood is focused on keeping the team up first, and then plans for the summer season.

Celtic hoped to keep Jason Denyer on loan from Manchester City next season. However, City's manager, Manuel Pellegrini, says his young players are not yet ready for the first team. This means Denyer might have to return to Manchester City instead of staying at Celtic.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a more accurate date before deciding if he needs to sign a new goalkeeper for the summer. Fraser Forster injured his knee during the 2-0 win over Burnley a fortnight ago, and doctors say he could be out for four to 12 months. Koeman does not want to give a precise timeline yet and trusts Kelvin Davis to cover for Forster, but he may have to bring a new keeper if Forster's recovery takes long.

Rotherham manager Steve Evans was angry on the sidelines after his team missed a penalty chance in a 1-0 loss to Birmingham City.

Birmingham scored first through Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Rotherham pulled a goal back through Matt Derbyshire. However, referee Dean Whitestone waved away appeals for a penalty after Rob Kiernan handled Matt Derbyshire clumsily near the hour mark.

Birmingham held out to win 1-0.

The worry about Virgil van Dijk is clear to see. Holland’s national team has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifying games than they gave up in the whole qualifying campaign for the last World Cup. And still, Guus Hiddink never calls or writes. The Celtic defender made it into two squads last year. But one step forward is usually followed by two steps back. When the Dutch were drawing 1-1 with Turkey the other night he was sunning himself in the Arabian Gulf and bumping into club-mates instead. Virgil van Dijk has been in fine form for Celtic but wasn't rewarded with a call-up to the Holland national team.

Celtic have complained to the SFA about ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final at Hampden this month.

The game is scheduled for 12.15pm on Sunday, April 18. Ticket prices are £23 for the North and South stands, and £15 for adults in the East Stand, with concessions at £5. Caley Thistle fans are unhappy because the match is scheduled before the first trains from Inverness arrive in Glasgow.

Rangers interim chairman Paul Murray says the club was forced to leave the stock market because of the previous board's mistakes. He insists the new board's plans and investments are safe and will go as planned.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were upset by their poor start against Italy on Tuesday. Just nine months after the World Cup, England played Italy in a friendly match in Turin. With high hopes after seven straight wins, England struggled in the first half. Italy took the lead with a header from Graziano Pelle. Despite the early goal, England captain Wayne Rooney kept his team level with a late equalizer to make the final score 1-1. Rooney said the team was upset by their first half performance.

Two of Dundee United's fan groups are angry about the club's leadership. They are shocked that 25% of the £6.3 million made from selling four players was paid as commission to unknown people. The groups also disagree with the chairman's investment in the team. In response, the board pointed to the team's success on the field.

Gary Locke will be confirmed as Kilmarnock's permanent manager on Friday. This happens exactly eight weeks after he was asked to lead the team until the end of the season. The Rugby Park club will make the announcement on Friday morning, and Locke—the former Hearts boss—will receive a three-year contract. On Thursday, the 39-year-old thanked the players who helped him win over new chairman Jim Mann, since he replaced Allan Johnston as a caretaker manager in February. Kilmarnock will confirm Gary Locke as the club's new permanent manager on Friday.

Chinese parents love having child prodigies. Some have 10-year-old children who are already in university, and others have four-year-olds who dance like Michael Jackson. Now, a new basketball superstar is becoming famous. A viral video from China shows a small boy with amazing basketball skills that would make many professional players feel ashamed. The boy is five years old and named Mai Zizhuo. He has been shooting hoops since he was two and a half years old, reported People's Daily Online. The video starts with the small player scoring many hoops before running around while dribbling two basketballs.

Bayern Munich will miss David Alaba for the rest of the season. The 22-year-old defender hurt his knee while playing for Austria on Tuesday. He tore a ligament, which will keep him out for about seven weeks. Earlier this year, Alaba was already out for three months with a partial knee injury. He said he is disappointed but he still hopes to play at the end of the season.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian forward Dane Tilse to replace the injured Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey. The 6ft 7in, 17st-plus Tilse has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract and will join the team as soon as paperwork arrives. The 30-year-old, who has made 200 appearances in Australia, will link up with his old teammate Terry Campese, the new Hull KR captain. He is a direct replacement for Weyman, who retired last month due to injury.

Livingston boss Mark Burchill thinks midfielder Darren Cole will play in Sunday's final, even though his cousin died last weekend. Shaun Cole, 22, was found dead in a Miami street; police think he was hit by a car. He was a soldier who served in Afghanistan and was on holiday in Florida. Burchill is hopeful Cole will play on Sunday.

Alan Smith has denied claims that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was traveling in after he broke his leg and dislocated his ankle in 2006.

Smith was injured while trying to block a free-kick from John Arne Riise during Manchester United's 1-0 defeat to Liverpool in the FA Cup. At the time of the incident, reports circulated that Liverpool fans tried to disrupt Smith's journey to hospital by throwing bottles, glasses and stones at the ambulance as well as rocking the vehicle.

C manager Ronny Deila says Celtic want to sign Danny Wilson. Wilson has one year left on his contract with Hearts. Celtic might offer £400,000 for him. Wilson used to play for Rangers and Liverpool. Hearts boss Ann Budge says they do not need to sell him.

Ronny Deila says Celtic will not travel to the United States or other countries this summer. He blames last year's trip to America, Austria, and Germany for a 4-1 loss to Legia Warsaw. Celtic usually plays pre-season games in other countries to make money, but they will not do that this year. A trip to America in July is still possible, but has not been decided on yet.

Franck Ribery has said reports linking Kevin de Bruyne to Bayern Munich are wrong. De Bruyne, who joined Wolfsburg from Chelsea, has had a great season, scoring nine goals and leading the league with 16 assists. However, Ribery believes De Bruyne's skills do not fit Bayern's style, as the Belgian player is different from himself and Arjen Robben.

The girlfriend of Arizona State University football player Davon Durant has recanted her story. She originally claimed he hit her and grabbed her neck during an argument in March 7, but she now says she lied because she was having mood swings. Durant was originally arrested and suspended from the football team after she accused him of domestic violence.

What is more exciting than meeting your idol? Meeting them at Starbucks while wearing a shirt with their name on it, and having your picture uploaded to their Instagram account.

One little boy was lucky enough to meet Justin Verlander, a pitcher for the Detroit Tigers, under those same, once-in-a-lifetime circumstances. Verlander snapped a selfie in front a little boy wearing a dark blue shirt with Verlander's name and jersey number, 35, on the back.

Eden Hazard said that playing too many games for Chelsea and Belgium might have made him too tired to play his best in Belgium's win over Israel on Tuesday. He has played 48 games this season but was taken off with 28 minutes left after struggling against Israel's defender Orel Dgani.

Police found 20 grams of marijuana hidden inside a leg of lamb in the Northern Territory. The lamb had been shipped to Darwin Airport and was going to be sent to the Tiwi Islands. Police became suspicious after something smelled strange, so they x-rayed the meat and found the drugs.

Troubled footballer Clarke Carlisle has revealed he has split from his wife. He is continuing to battle with depression after he tried to kill himself in December. The former Premier League defender said he has moved out of the marital home in Yorkshire. He shared the home with his wife of 14 years, Gemma. Mr Carlisle was arrested on suspicion of drink-driving two days before he tried to kill himself.

Arsenal legend Paul Merson criticized Andros Townsend's England call-up. However, Townsend scored an equalizer in England's 1-1 draw with Italy on Tuesday. This goal proved Merson wrong, as it was a great response to his comments.

It seems that Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas is struggling this season. He was one of the worst players in Spain's 2-0 loss to Holland on Tuesday. The 27-year-old said he was happy in London earlier this week, but his performance has gotten much worse. In December, he was playing so well that he looked like he would break the Premier League assist record.

Six people have been arrested in Dover on suspicion of Syria-related terrorism offences. Five men and one woman were detained at around 8:00 this morning in the departure zone of the south coast port. Four of the men are from Birmingham, West Midlands, and are in their 20s. A 26-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman with no fixed address were also held. The six people are currently being questioned at a police station in the West Midlands area.

Get ready to dig deep—the impulse to buy a treat peaks today at 12:52 PM. A study claims that Britons spend an average of £62 a week on rewarding themselves, with retail therapy reaching a high at lunchtime today. Treats can range from a bar of chocolate to a glass of wine. And surprisingly, men spend a third more a month than women on treating themselves.

Arsene Wenger is very respected and clearly a very smart man. Sometimes, you might agree with him, but looking closer shows his ideas usually have weak foundations. Usually, he talks about Arsenal's defense stats, which are actually very good. But last week, he talked about quotas. He talked about FA chairman Greg Dyke’s idea to increase the number of homegrown players in a Premier League squad of 25 from eight to 12.

Charlie Austin and Joey Barton are now good friends. On his first day at Queens Park Rangers, Barton ignored Austin. Later, Barton realized he had made a mistake and the two became close. Austin had a great first Premier League season. He scored 15 goals and might play for England in the future.

This dog is a true hero. He saved his owner from a cold and muddy grave at the dam in Springfield, Ohio. The black dog took a rescue rope out to the man, who was waist-deep in mud trying to get his duck hunting gear. Firefighters pulled the man to safety. He had called 911 on his cell phone, but the water was too shallow for a boat to reach him.

Juventus coach Massimiliano Allegri says he will only be fully accepted by the fans if he wins the league title. He joined the team last summer, replacing Antonio Conte. Since then, Juventus is leading the race for the Scudetto. They play Empoli on Saturday looking for three points.

Nathan Redmond had only been on the pitch for six minutes when he scored the winning goal. Steven Whittaker passed the ball to Redmond down the right side of the field. Redmond ran past the defender and crossed the ball into the net, giving his team a 2-0 lead.

For years, people in Celoron, New York have been upset about a statue of Lucile Ball. In 2009, the town put up a statue of Ball that looks very unlike her. The face looks bad, and people are shocked and mad. A Facebook page called 'We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue' has gotten more than 600 likes. The statue is based on a famous moment from Ball's show 'I Love Lucy,' in which she pitches an intoxicating health tonic while drunk.

South Sydney hooker Issac Luke is in trouble after he posted a homophobic comment on social media. The 27-year-old had asked for help finding a Rabbitohs fan who was allegedly attacked at ANZ Stadium. He wanted to give the fan a jersey to make up for the incident, but the comment he posted online caused the problem.

Arachnophobes beware - the following will make your blood run cold. A Victorian driver got a rude shock when a massive huntsman crawled out from inside his door handle. The spine-tinging video, which was captured in Wangaratta, northeast Victoria, begins with the man approaching his black Holden Ute and spraying the door with an insect repellent. The driver sprays his car with insect repellent, forcing a huntsman spider to reveal itself from under the door handle. ‘Get out, you bast**’, he stoically says to the spider. But the man appears less composed when the hairy huntsman’s legs pop out, yelping and cowering back in fright.

Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino says Harry Kane is like Gabriel Batistuta. Kane moved close to scoring 30 goals for the season after playing for England against Lithuania. Roy Hodgson is keeping expectations low for Kane. Kane started in the England team after playing on loan at Norwich and Leicester.

A former footballer named Michael McIndoe ran a £30 million investment scheme. He promised other footballers a 20% return on their money. However, the scheme collapsed because of mounting debts, and McIndoe was declared bankrupt in October with over £2 million in debt. He is known for living a millionaire's lifestyle in Marbella, but he is now surviving on handouts as creditors chase him through the courts.

Juventus director Pavel Nedved said Barcelona want to sign Paul Pogba. In an interview, the former midfielder, who played 324 games for Juventus, said Pogba will not move. However, Nedved was happy Juventus did not play Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals.

A 48-year-old convicted sex offender named James Oliver was hit by a car driven by his girlfriend, Linda Currier, 53. Police say Currier hit Oliver with her car after she caught him allegedly sexually assaulting a 12-year-old girl inside their home. Oliver suffered a serious leg injury and was found in the driveway of a home in Noblesboro, Maine.

Liverpool is interested in Fiorentina goalkeeper Neto, but the player is also wanted by Paris Saint-Germain and Spanish clubs. Brendan Rodgers is having difficult competition to sign the 25-year-old, whose contract ends in June. Liverpool was linked with a move for Neto earlier in the season when Simon Mignolet was dropped. A January transfer did not happen, but Neto is likely to leave Fiorentina in the summer.

Not everyone can drive a $50,000 car. A YouTube video shows a Porsche Cayman speeding from a green light on Prince Edward Island in Canada. The car swerved wildly and hit a concrete median. A wheel even came off before the car stopped. The video says, "Just cause you have a nice car doesn't make you a good driver. Don't let your son drive your Porsche!"

Here is the information you need for Sunday's Sunderland vs Newcastle game:

Sunderland's midfielder Lee Cattermole will start in the game. He is returning from a two-match ban after getting 10 yellow cards this season. Manager Dick Advocaat confirmed he is fit to play.

If Rory McIlroy wins the Masters tournament, he will complete a career grand slam and achieve his lifelong goal as the world's best golfer. Working with his sponsor Bose, McIlroy released a video showing his journey from playing on the backyard as a child to conquering the golfing world. The video starts with McIlroy going for a morning jog while the tagline 'Six weeks to Georgia' appears on the screen. It also includes an interview with a young Rory McIlroy before he became a golfing superstar.

Sergio Garcia says he is focused on winning his first PGA Tour title since 2012 at this week's Shell Houston Open. Even though the Masters tournament is coming up soon, and people have been talking about Rory McIlroy trying to win a third major in a row, and whether Tiger Woods will end his self-imposed break from golf, and other topics. But Garcia is only concentrating on ending his victory drought.

Sergio Garcia lines up a putt during the Cadillac Championship in Doral, Florida last month.

Riki Hughes, a veteran of the Iraq war, stole £17,000 from the football club where he volunteered as secretary. He lied to the team, saying he was paying rent, but the club actually got the property for free. Hughes spent the money on equipment and a stag party in Las Vegas. He was jailed for 16 months by Salisbury Crown Court.

Johnny Sexton is very successful. He has won trophies every year since he started playing at a senior level in 2010. As he gets ready for a big game in Paris, he reflected on his lucky habit. He said he has been part of great teams with Leinster and Ireland, and almost every year he has been part of a team that won trophies.

Mustafa Kamal quit as ICC president on Wednesday. He said India used its position to influence the outcome of the Cricket World Cup quarter-final against Bangladesh.

"Everyone saw what happened during the Bangladesh-India match ... India has influenced the outcome of the match using its position (in the ICC)," Kamal, a Bangladeshi, said at the airport on his return from the tournament in Australia. "From now on, I am a former president of the ICC. I would have reacted similarly had it happened to any other country."

Mustafa Kamal, pictured with the Cricket World Cup trophy, has stepped down as ICC President.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce supports Nigel Pearson. Allardyce was Pearson's boss when Pearson worked at Newcastle United in 2007. Allardyce thinks Pearson is "his own man." They will be reunited on Saturday when West Ham plays Leicester at the King Power Stadium. Pearson has had several controversial moments this year, including grabbing James McArthur by the throat and arguing with a reporter.

Skipper John O'Shea has challenged Sunderland to win their next derby against Newcastle. This will be their fifth win in a row against Newcastle. Sunderland plays at the Stadium of Light on Sunday. They have won the last four games against Newcastle, but they really need three points to help them stay safe from the battle to stay in the Premier League.

O'Shea and his team could end in the relegation zone if Burnley beat Tottenham on Sunday. If that happens, three points become a necessity.

Stoke boss Mark Hughes says his team must stop their bad run at Chelsea. Since 2008, Stoke have played Chelsea eight times and lost every game. They last won there in 1995, but before that, the only draw was a 1-1 game in 1984. Chelsea recently beat Stoke 3-0.

Newcastle will play Sunderland on Sunday. They want to avoid a third loss in a row. The team has struggled recently without their banned striker, Papiss Cisse. Sunderland is at the bottom of the league table. However, without Cisse’s goals, Newcastle would be two points behind the drop zone. Cisse is Newcastle’s top scorer this year with 11 goals. Ten of those goals have helped his team win games.

Dick Advocaat will welcome Lee Cattermole back to the Sunderland team. Cattermole has been suspended for the last two games, but he is fit to play against Newcastle on Sunday. He missed a large part of the season through injury before his suspension. Advocaat wants Cattermole to do well in this important game.

For Ronny Deila, playing in the Champions League is not just about the money. However, there are now 16 million reasons for the Norwegian to lead Celtic to a fourth straight title. All of these reasons involve pound signs. This week, UEFA confirmed their 'cash cycle' for the next three years of European competition. The last time Celtic reached the Champions League group stage, in 2013-14 when they faced AC Milan, Ajax and Barcelona, they won one match and earned £12.6m. If they perform the same – or better – next season, that sum would rise by £4m. If they reach the last 16, the figures would crash through the £20m barrier. And that is even before ticket sales

Tottenham defender Ben Davies will play against his teammate Sam Vokes at Burnley on Sunday. Spurs are looking to keep up their good form, having lost only once this season before the international break. They want to keep their hopes of playing in Europe alive. Burnley are in trouble, sitting in 18th place, just one point away from the drop zone. Vokes previously scored against Tottenham in the FA Cup, but Davies was unhappy about the result.

Neil Redfearn is thinking about his job as manager of Leeds United after the club suspended his assistant, Steve Thompson. Leeds hired Thompson two months ago, but they told him yesterday that he is suspended until the end of the season, ending his time at the club after 105 days. Thompson has been told his contract will not be renewed. Leeds United assistant manager Steve Thompson has been suspended by the club.

John Carver says he will use a whip if he has to to motivate his Newcastle players ahead of Sunday's Tyne-Wear derby at the Stadium of Light. The Magpies have lost the last four matches against their North-East rivals and head coach Carver – who was assistant to Alan Pardew during that wretched run – admits that Sunderland wanted victory more than United on those occasions. 'In the last four games Sunderland have out-worked us - and that's not a good stat to have,' he said. John Carver says he will 'whip' his players to make sure they're motivated to beat Sunderland on Sunday.

David Templeton has strongly criticized the training methods used at Rangers by Ally McCoist and Kenny McDowall. He says former manager Stuart McCall brought a better style of coaching and preparation. Templeton praised McCall for the positive impact he has made since arriving last month, with back-to-back wins reviving confidence ahead of Saturday's home game against Championship title-winners Hearts.

Celta Vigo forward Nolito says Lionel Messi should go to the Spanish coast on Sunday instead of playing in their La Liga game.

Messi has a minor foot injury but is expected to recover in time to play. Yesterday, he trained with his teammate Javier Mascherano. Nolito, who is 28, urged Messi to stay away. He said, "I guess he'll come, but he can spend the day at the beach as far as I'm concerned. I'll give his dad a ring in a minute."

Robbie Neilson says Hearts captain Danny Wilson will only leave the club if the manager is happy with the deal. Speaking ahead of a game against Rangers, Neilson admitted that other teams are interested in his players. However, he will only let them go if he thinks it is the right move for Hearts.

Sam Allardyce has warned Brendan Rodgers that giving Raheem Sterling a new contract could cause other Liverpool players to demand higher wages. He feels paying Sterling more than the current £100,000-per-week offer would set a bad example for the young squad. Allardyce does not blame Sterling for wanting more money, but believes clubs are overpaying talented young players because there are too few emerging talents. Raheem Sterling, who currently earns £35,000 a week at Liverpool, has not yet agreed to a new deal.

Blackpool are trying to sign 25-year-old Austria defender Thomas Piermayr. He is a free agent who used to play for Colorado Rapids. He has never played in England before, but Blackpool want to give him his first chance in English football.

Tony Pulis wants to talk to West Bromwich Albion's chairman, Jeremy Peace, after the team stays in the Premier League. Pulis says the team has gotten off track recently and needs big changes to return to the top ten. West Brom finished 10th and 8th under previous managers Roy Hodgson and Steve Clarke. Last season, the team struggled to stay in the league and finished 17th.

Arsenal legend Ian Wright is sad that Theo Walcott might leave north London. Wright thinks Walcott's problems at the club are because manager Arsene Wenger wouldn't play him as a striker. Walcott has only started five games this season after coming back from a seven-month injury. With Arsenal looking for Raheem Sterling and Walcott's contract ending next summer, Wright worries the team could lose a valuable player.

Roberto Martinez believes Ross Barkley is ready to play better after the midfielder recovered from a knee injury and two substitute appearances for England. Barkley had a difficult season following the World Cup and missing out on domestic games. However, England manager Roy Hodgson has kept faith in him, and Martinez now believes Barkley can become a better player for Everton and England.

England will not play in the Under 19 European Championships this summer. The Young Lions lost 2-1 to France in their final qualifier. They had already beaten Denmark and Azerbaijan, but needed to beat France in Saint-Lo to advance to the finals in Greece. Goals from Sehrou Guirassy and Gnaly Cornet put France in command, and a late goal from Patrick Roberts was not enough to rescue the team.

Newcastle midfielder Jonas Gutierrez is hoping to celebrate his return to the first team with a win over struggling Sunderland. The 31-year-old Argentinian has played as a substitute in the last three games since returning from cancer. He has been welcomed back warmly. However, he has lost each of those games. He is desperate to end that run as Newcastle try to bounce back from four successive defeats by their rivals at the Stadium of Light on Sunday.

NRL referees and officials were hit with plastic water bottles and abuse by angry fans after South Sydney beat Canterbury 18-17 in a controversial match on Good Friday at ANZ Stadium. The Rabbitohs won when the referee penalised Canterbury captain James Graham in the final minute. As players and officials left the field, a section of the crowd threw bottles and shouted abuse at them.

Kevin Sinfield, the former England captain, has announced he will leave rugby league at the end of the season to join Yorkshire Carnegie. The 34-year-old is considered the greatest captain in Leeds' history. He made the surprise decision on Tuesday.

Raheem Sterling, a 20-year-old winger for Liverpool, has said he is not ready to sign a new contract. He was offered £100,000 a week to stay at Anfield, but he revealed on Wednesday that he would have signed for much less money a year ago.

Although he is a key player for Liverpool, Sterling has struggled to repeat last season's impressive form. He has scored only six goals this campaign, one less than Stoke's Jon Walters. His scoring rate and time per goal have also gotten worse.

Brighton and Hove Albion are giving their young players training on the law and ethics of sexual consent. The Championship club is the first to provide this training to its youth players, according to the BBC. The " Protect, Inform and Prevent " program explains when consent can legally be given. Part of the training involves confidential question and answer sessions about past encounters, led by a former police detective and a psychotherapist.

A new video shows homeless people reading cruel tweets written about them. The clip, made by the agency Leo Burnett Toronto for the charity Humans For Humans, is meant to make people think about how they treat people sleeping rough. Many of the people break down in tears as they read mean comments like, 'I hate the homeless, I don’t feel sorry for you,' and 'I saw a homeless girl across the street. I almost vomited.'

George Boyd is the Barclays Premier League's hardest working player. He ran 210.5 miles this season, which is the same distance as running from Burnley's Turf Moor ground to Crystal Palace's Selhurst Park in south London. He ran slightly further than Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Christian Eriksen. Walking that distance would usually take 69 hours, but Boyd has managed it in less than 40 hours of playing time.

Police investigating the death of a five-month-old baby have arrested the child's parents. The father, 25, and mother, 25, from Perry Barr, Birmingham, were held after their daughter died yesterday afternoon. Police were called to their home just before 1am yesterday morning because the baby was said to be suffering breathing difficulties. A baby was found dead at this home in Perry Barr, Birmingham yesterday afternoon. The child was taken to Birmingham Children's Hospital but died hours later. A spokesman for West Midlands Police said: 'The death is being treated as suspicious; a post mortem will take place today to establish the exact cause of death.'

Gordon Taylor, the leader of the players' union, says Raheem Sterling is not being disloyal to Liverpool by waiting to talk about a new contract until the summer. The 20-year-old England player has been offered a huge new deal, believed to be £100,000-a-week, but talks have stopped. Sterling says he is not motivated by money, and Taylor thinks waiting until the season is over is a smart idea. Sterling also admitted in a TV interview that he is not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool.

Things have been bad for Manchester United flop Anderson since he went back to Brazil. On Wednesday, his own mistakes were hidden by his teammate's stupidity. The midfielder got a red card for shoving an opponent. But his teammate Fabrício got a red card too for swearing at the fans, leaving Internacional with nine men in the 1-1 game in Porto Alegre.

A seven-year-old boy was raped and set on fire by two youths when he went to buy food. The youths took the boy to an isolated place and raped him. When he resisted, they set him on fire. The boy, who suffered 30 percent burns to his body, somehow escaped. The shocking incident occurred in Pagma Nagar, in Bhiwandi City, a suburb of Mumbai. Police are investigating the incident.

Jose Mourinho could one day return to manage Real Madrid, even after he left the club in 2013. Real defender Alvaro Arbeloa says the door is never closed to the Chelsea manager. Mourinho spent three years at Real Madrid before returning to Chelsea. He left because of arguments with star players like Iker Casillas and Sergio Ramos. Even though he left under bad terms, Arbeloa says Real Madrid might want him back one day.

Liverpool's hopes of playing in the Champions League ended on Saturday at the Emirates. The manager, Brendan Rodgers, admitted his team's chances were over during a 15-minute press conference. Even though he tried to stay positive, Rodgers does not act gloary. But he admitted this has been a tough season. Last year, Liverpool played for the title, but this year they have slipped out of contention. It is a sad feeling for a club that hoped for a return to glory. Even so, it still feels like Liverpool are moving forward under Rodgers.

Inter Milan coach Roberto Mancini was angry after his team drew 1-1 with Parma on Saturday. He cancelled the players' day off and made them train early on Sunday morning. Inter confirmed the training started at 8:30 a.m. Javier Zanetti and Piero Ausilio watched the session.

Foc fans want to own a piece of sports history. Rare items linked to favorite players or teams can sell for thousands of pounds. A old passport belonging to former Manchester United and England player Paul Parker was listed on eBay with a £5,000 price tag. The bidding ended on Tuesday, but it is not known if anyone paid that price.

A man has been spotted seeing Jesus' face in toast, pancakes, and crisps, and even ice cream. But a builder was surprised when he saw Jesus Christ on a piece of wood just days before Easter. Paddy Morrall noticed the full-length picture of Christ on a snapped scaffolding board in Inverness, Scotland, on Wednesday. The son of God appeared wearing a robe after the joiner and colleagues left the piece of wood out in the rain for several hours. The 31-year-old builder, from Keighley, near Bradford, has kept the board.

Ondrej Duda scored one goal in the second half to give Slovakia a 1-0 win over the Czech Republic on Tuesday. The 20-year-old midfielder scored with a low shot from outside the penalty area in the 49th minute. This was Slovakia's third win in ten matches since the countries split in 1993. Martin Skrtel hit Daniel Kolar in the face with a high boot during the game. Slovakia continues their excellent recent form with this victory.

Real Madrid star Karim Benzema showed off his rapping skills while driving his Bugatti Veyron. He sang along to Tupac's song 'Check Out Time' as the team gets ready to play Granada on Sunday. Benzema, who has scored 20 goals this season, looks like he wants to add more to his total.

A businessman who helped force a government minister to resign is spending money to defeat two Conservative Party candidates.

Harvey Boulter, a supporter of the Ukip party, has given £30,000 to help defeat Liam Fox in his constituency. He is also spending another £30,000 to try to defeat Tom Tugendhat in Kent.

Two goals in the last four minutes made the match between Sheffield Wednesday and Huddersfield end in a 1-1 draw.

Sergiu Bus scored for Wednesday in the 86th minute. Ishmael Miller scored for Huddersfield just 60 seconds later. The result means Huddersfield has not won in seven games and stays in 18th place, nine points behind Wednesday.

Stuart Dallas has come a long way since Mark Warburton found him playing part-time for £70 a week. The 23-year-old had a great week with Northern Ireland and scored two amazing goals as Brentford beat Fulham 4-1 on Good Friday. They go into Monday's game against Nottingham Forest wanting more than just a play-off spot. It was three years ago when Dallas was spotted by Warburton playing on a mud bath for Crusaders back home. Stuart Dallas celebrates the second of his two excellent goals against Fulham on good Friday . Dallas has been a revelation this season as he helps Brentford push towards the Premier League .

Baseball is very popular in America. People have strong feelings about their favorite teams. The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox are the most popular teams, coming in first and second. The Texas Rangers and Atlanta Braves also have many fans in the South. Some teams, like the New York Mets, are not as popular.

A basketball player named Trey Moses asked a girl named Ellie Meredith to be his date for the upcoming school prom. Moses, who helps students with learning disabilities, gave Ellie flowers and a sign that said, "Let's Party Like it's 1989." Ellie loves the singer Taylor Swift. Ellie said yes and told a news channel that she is excited to go dress shopping because she has told many people about it.

On April Fools' Day, President Barack Obama pretended to be Frank Underwood, the fake president from the TV show *House of Cards*.

He spoke in a southern accent and pretended to talk to the camera like the character does in the show. "Hello everybody. This is not Frank Underwood," the president said. "This is Barack Obama. Happy April Fools' Day. Frank learned it from me," he joked.

President Barack Obama impersonated House of Cards' fictional president Frank Underwood by dipping into a southern drawl .

Caykur Rizespor midfielder Ludovic Obraniak went to the hospital on Saturday after he felt unwell during a game against Fenerbahce. He was taken for tests after being substituted at halftime. The club said preliminary tests showed he was not in immediate danger. Obraniak is on loan from German club Werder Bremen.

Three people went to the hospital after a crash on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney.

The accident happened at a traffic light intersection when a 1973 vintage sports car, a Jaguar, hit a Toyota Kluger 4WD. The Jaguar was completely wrecked. All three adults in the cars were taken to the hospital as a precaution, though nobody was actually hurt. Police are still investigating how the crash happened.

Villagers from Shandong Province in eastern China have reportedly resorted to transporting natural gas in plastic bags. Recent images show intrepid residents from Lijin village in Dongying city carry the explosive in bags as long as six metres on rickshaws, reported the People’s Daily Online. Worried passers-by compared this behaviour to carrying a bomb on their backs because any contact with a naked flame or even a cigarette could spell disaster. Gas-guzzler: Carrying natural gas in huge plastic bags is a common scene in some villages in Shandong . Penny-pinching: Local media suggest this is a way for villages to save money on the transportation of gas .
