Tiger Woods has been seen practicing at Augusta National, raising hopes he will play in this year's first Major. Woods has not played on the PGA Tour since he withdrew from an tournament in February because of back problems. He has been taking a break to get back in shape, but there is talk he will return for the Masters, a tournament he has won four times. Tiger Woods was spotted practising at Augusta on Tuesday and is said to have returned to the course . Woods has dropped out of the top 100 for the first time in almost 19 years .

The BBC has faced criticism for using licence fee payers' money to pay for a 44-page guide teaching staff how to use emojis. The BBC's executives hired an agency to research how smiley faces could be used in news and on social media. Emoji designers were also asked to make graphics for popular stars like Gary Lineker and Graham Norton. The BBC was also accused of using a 'sad face' emoticon to describe the death of the world's oldest woman.

One of the world's top distance runners says he is living in fear of his life. He claims a coach in Uganda has been sexually abcing young female runners, some as young as 15. Moses Kipsiro, a Commonwealth Games champion, says five runners came to him for help. He claims he has since received death threats after reporting the allegations to his national federation and the police.

Former Holland forward and assistant coach Patrick Kluivert has had a winning start as coach of Curacao. The Caribbean island team advanced to the second qualifying round in CONCACAF for the 2018 tournament late Tuesday. Curacao drew 2-2 in a second-leg match at Montserrat to win 4-3 on aggregate. Kluivert's team won 2-1 on Saturday in Willemstad. Patrick Kluivert has helped Curacao progress to the next stage of 2018 World Cup qualification. Former Holland assistant Kluivert (far right) worked with Louis van Gaal (centre) at the 2014 World Cup.

An 18-year-old student has been kicked out of his fraternity, left college, and sent for a mental check after he was filmed biting the head off a live hamster. DailyMail.com found him last weekend. He is the stepsson of a former Mississippi governor candidate. The video is from a drunken Spring Break party in Florida. In the video, he shrieked with laughter as he killed the animal. He could be charged with animal cruelty. This crime has a maximum jail term of five years and a $5,000 fine.

Sri Lanka's sports minister asked Kumar Sangakkara to keep playing limited overs cricket for one more year. Sangakkara had retired on March 18 after a quarter-final loss, saying he was happy with how the team had improved since 2000.

Edinburgh is welcoming back three Scottish international players for their European Challenge Cup quarter-final match against London Irish on Sunday. Dougie Fife, Alasdair Dickinson, and Ross Ford were rested last week during a 26-15 win over Scarlets. They are now back with the team because head coach Alan Solomons wants to pick his strongest starting team. Dougie Fife is one of the retretned players returning to Edinburgh after playing for Scotland in the Six Nations.

Chris Ramsey says Tony Pulis is one of the best British coaches in the country. But he insists his team, QPR, doesn't need tactical advice from the experienced "relegation" expert.

QPR are 19th in the Premier League, four points behind Sunderland in 17th. The team has only taken four points since the new year started. They could use a late-season surge like the one Pulis led with Crystal Palace in 2013-14, where he took 17 points from the final eight games to keep them from being relegated.

Chris Ramsey praised Tony Pulis ahead of his sides crucial clash with West Brom in the Premier League.

An 18-year-old student named Silhan Ozcelik appeared in court. She is accused of planning to travel abroad to join Kurdish rebels fighting against Islamic State. She is 18 years old and went missing from her family's home in north London last October, while she was still only 17. The court heard that she travelled on the Eurostar with a man to Stuttgart, Germany, where the Kurdish Workers' Party youth movement have its headquarters.
